newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA 3.37 MLN T WHEAT HARVEST TOPS ESTIMATES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA 3.37 MLN T WHEAT HARVEST TOPS ESTIMATES.

text.p: Bulgaria's 3.375 million tonnes of bread wheat harvested from nearly 90 percent of sown areas so far will cover domestic consumption, an Agriculture ministry official said on Tuesday.
"We have collected 3.375 million tonnes of wheat from harvested 107,884 hectares which is 88 percent of the sown areas," Agriculture ministry spokeswoman told reporters.
"We do not expect any problems in meeting Bulgaria's bread wheat consumption with domestic production," she added.
She said the average yield was 3.13 tonnes per hectare, higher than the previously estimated two tonnes per hectare.
At this yield Bulgaria may harvest 3.8 million tonnes of wheat from a total of 1.225 million hectares sown, up from 2.4 million tonnes estimated by the ministry in May.
State firms have bought some 600,000 tonnes of bread wheat from this years crop by mid-August out of planned 800,000 tonnes, Farm ministry figures showed.
A further 300,000 tonnes were bought by private mills and traders.
Bulgaria's annual consumption is estimated at 1.6 million tonnes of bread wheat and 800,000 tonnes of feed wheat.

The cabinet lowered on Monday state quality standarts for bread wheat until October 15 as heavy rainfall delayed the harvest in Bulgaria's northwest major production regions and the wheat started to germinate.
The wheat harvest deadline for Bulgaria is end-July and around 150,000 hectares have not been harvested yet.
The government introduced on Monday a minimum purchase price for second and third quality bread wheat at 210,000 levs and 190,000 levs respectively in a move to support local producers.
The minimum purchase price for first quality wheat was set at 230,000 levs for this year.
Bulgaria has to export some 232,000 tonnes of wheat this year under futures contracts agreed earlier this year. Poland has said it could accept cash payment for 100,000 of the total.
An export fee of 15 percent of international wheat prices was set in a bid to curb exports.
Bulgaria has collected 825,339 tonnes of barley from harvested 98 percent of the sown areas up from 450,000 tonnes last year, Farm ministry figures showed.
The country's annual consumption is estimated at around 870,000 tonnes of brewery and feed barley but agriculture experts say Bulgaria was unlikely to need imports until the 1998 crop.

"Possible feed barley shortage could be compensated by feed maize and Bulgaria may not need to import barley until next year," Svetla Bachvarova from the state Agricultural Market Information System told Reuters. -- Ivan Mastagarkov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
